measurements.system_model: Study CS6 (APPROACH) phase 3 trial in FCS

measurements.effect_vs_control: Measured null: the applicant looked for a relationship between bleeding events and platelet level, and between bleeding events and antiplatelet/anticoagulant co-medication, and found none
measurements.source_locus: Section 2.6.1 clinical safety, Study CS6 adverse events narrative, PDF p.86 (text lines 6512-6514)

measurements.notes: ABSENCE ROW (measured null). This is the key dissociation finding for volanesorsen: bleeding is NOT explained by the thrombocytopenia. Included under the coagulation endpoint because the source uses it to argue for a cascade (contact-pathway/tenase) rather than platelet mechanism; no platelet count is extracted here.

measurements.system_model: Study CS6 (APPROACH) phase 3 trial in FCS
measurements.control_description: NOT_APPLICABLE (mechanistic attribution, not a measurement)
measurements.effect_vs_control: Assessor/applicant mechanistic attribution of the injection-site bleeding excess to a transient local disruption of the contact pathway, with a separate systemic ASO effect on the tenase complex
measurements.source_locus: Section 2.6.1 clinical safety, Study CS6 adverse events narrative, PDF p.86 (text lines 6505-6508)
measurements.verbatim_quote: Bleeding events were reported in 16 (49%) patients in the volanesorsen group compared with 4 (12%) patients in the placebo group. Nearly half of these events were local to the injection site, which may be a result of the known transient effect of ASOs on the tenase complex.
measurements.notes: QUALITATIVE MECHANISM ROW - the numbers in the quote duplicate the Table 42 row above; what this row carries is the attribution of injection-site bleeding to the known transient ASO effect on the TENASE COMPLEX (intrinsic FVIIIa/FIXa). The CHMP restates it at PDF pp.102-103 with the additional contact-pathway claim, but that sentence is split by a page break in the text layer ('...a transient disruption of the contact' | page header | 'pathway, while antisense oligonucleotides are known to affect the tenase complex, although the last effect is more considered a systemic effect.'), so the contiguous p.86 sentence is quoted instead. NO coagulation assay result is reported anywhere in this dossier to support the contact-pathway/tenase claim - see extraction_notes.

extraction_notes:
SCOPE. Bundle z-human-ema-epar, 8 regulatory documents covering four approved oligonucleotides in humans: volanesorsen (EMA CHMP AR + EU-RMP v3.0 + Product Information), inotersen (EMA CHMP AR + FDA NDA 211172 Medical and Clinical Pharmacology Reviews), donidalorsen (EMA CHMP AR) and vutrisiran (EMA CHMP AR). All 70 measurement rows are human (species='human'); 69 are study_type='clinical' and 1 is 'ex_vivo_human_plasma' (the donidalorsen CS2 extended coagulation/fibrinolysis panel).

THE HEADLINE FINDING - VOLANESORSEN HAS NO CASCADE ASSAY DATA AT ALL. This was the bundle's priority target. The three volanesorsen documents together contain ZERO measurements of aPTT, PT, thrombin time, fibrinogen, D-dimer, antithrombin, anti-Xa, thrombin generation or any coagulation factor activity. I ran whitespace-normalised searches for every one of those terms across all three files: 'partial thromboplastin' 0 hits, 'prothrombin' 0 hits, 'thrombin time' 0 hits, 'fibrinogen' 0 hits, 'd-dimer' 0 hits, 'antithrombin' 0 hits, 'anti-xa' 0 hits, 'thrombin generation' 0 hits. The ONLY clotting-time datum in the entire volanesorsen dossier is a single treatment-emergent 'International normalised ratio increased' event in 1 patient (1%), which the SmPC then carries as a labelled Common adverse reaction (and the package leaflet renders as 'an increase in blood clotting time'). This is REGULATORY/REPORTING SILENCE, not a measured null, and per the extraction rules I did NOT write silence rows for the unmeasured analytes because I cannot quote a sentence that proves an absence of measurement. Reviewers must not read the volanesorsen bleeding rows as implying a normal coagulation screen - no screen was published.

WHY THE SILENCE MATTERS. Both the CHMP AR and the EU-RMP attribute volanesorsen's injection-site bleeding excess to specific cascade mechanisms - 'a transient disruption of the contact pathway' and 'the known transient effect of ASOs on the tenase complex' - and then publish no assay of either. Two mechanistic claims about the intrinsic pathway and the FVIIIa/FIXa tenase complex are made in an approved product's assessment report with no supporting aPTT, factor VIII/IX activity or thrombin generation data anywhere in the dossier. Both mechanism statements are captured as qualitative rows (readout_value NOT_REPORTED, readout_is_qualitative true) precisely so a downstream reader can see the claim and its unsupported status together.

CONTRADICTIONS FOUND (all recorded, none silently reconciled):
(1) Volanesorsen bleeding incidence. The Waylivra AR gives THREE different pooled/per-study figures: 49% vs 12% for CS6 (p.86 and Table 42, 16/33 vs 4/33), 36% vs 14% for the pooled phase 3 placebo-controlled studies (p.102), and 28% vs 16% for CS16 (p.112). A fourth figure, '49% vs 12% ... with approximately 3 events vs 1 event per patient', appears in section 3.4 attributed to the pooled population. Rows exist for the CS6, pooled and CS16 values as printed.
(2) Donidalorsen Pool 2 bleeding TEAEs. Section 2.6.8.2 (p.146) says 17.8% for the 80 mg every-4-weeks group; section 2.6.8.9 (p.167) says 14.7% for the same group in the same pool. Irreconcilable from the published text. BOTH are recorded as separate rows, explicitly cross-referenced.
(3) Donidalorsen CS2 prekallikrein depth. -64.7% nadir at Day 85 (p.57) versus 'approximately 60% from Baseline on Day 113' (p.74). Different timepoints, so not strictly incompatible, but the two passages are not cross-referenced.
(4) Donidalorsen exposure-adjusted bleeding rates are labelled 'per 100 patient years of exposure' and then printed with '%' signs (15.5%, 5.7%, 26.2%). A unit error in the source; preserved as printed with the source's own unit wording in readout_unit.
(5) Inotersen anticoagulant co-medication. The CS2 analysis and the Effects Table both state no increase in bleeding with anticoagulants; the CS3 open-label narrative reports 33% vs 24%. Both recorded.
(6) Inotersen haematoma/subdermal bleeds. The AR prints '(20.5% and 11.7%)' and says the difference favours placebo, but the preceding pair in the same sentence is ordered placebo-then-inotersen, which would make the second pair mean the opposite. The source does not label the two values. Recorded UNASSIGNED: both numbers appear in readout_value and control_value, direction taken from the words. FDA Table 45 (Study CS2 Hemorrhage TEAEs) would settle it but is an image with no text layer in the converted file.
(7) Vutrisiran GalNAc attachment point. The AR states at p.14 that GalNAc is on the 3' end of the ANTISENSE strand, but the printed chemical name puts it on the sense strand 3'-adenylate and the non-clinical section says sense strand. Recorded as sense strand and flagged in the oligo notes.

WHAT THE BUNDLE ACTUALLY CONTRIBUTES BEYOND THE VOLANESORSEN GAP. The strongest positive human dataset here is donidalorsen: an approved oligonucleotide whose TARGET IS A COAGULATION CONTACT-SYSTEM ZYMOGEN (plasma prekallikrein). It gives paired on-target depth and cascade safety in the same humans - 93.6% PKK depletion and 98.6% loss of plasma proenzyme activation in healthy volunteers, 73.4% PKK depletion versus +2.1% on placebo in the phase 3 trial - alongside a scheduled aPTT/PT/INR/D-dimer panel with no trend, a dedicated 22-patient ex vivo extended coagulation and fibrinolysis panel unchanged from baseline, no thrombotic AESIs, and an exposure-adjusted bleeding rate BELOW placebo. That is the cleanest human on-target-versus-toxicity pairing in the bundle. Inotersen supplies the class's index severe-bleeding event (one fatal intracranial haemorrhage at a platelet nadir <10 x 10^9/L) together with an explicit measured null on aPTT/INR/PT. Vutrisiran supplies a GalNAc-siRNA negative control (aPTT/PT/INR stable).

THREE INDEPENDENT REGULATORY EXCLUSIONS OF CONSUMPTIVE COAGULOPATHY. The Waylivra RMP (volanesorsen), the Tegsedi AR (inotersen, EMA) and the FDA Clinical Pharmacology Review (inotersen, FDA) each separately investigated and excluded DIC, TTP and thrombotic microangiopathy as the mechanism of 2'-MOE gapmer thrombocytopenia. Three absence rows, three different assessors, two different sponsors. Together with the matched finding in both programmes that bleeding events do NOT correlate with platelet count, this is the most reusable conclusion in the bundle.

CONVENTIONS AND LIMITS.
- VERBATIM QUOTES: every quote was verified programmatically against the source file after collapsing all runs of whitespace to single spaces (PDF text layers wrap mid-sentence). No other alteration was made. PDF artefacts are preserved as printed and flagged in notes where they look like typos: 'Haemorrh ages', 'no- coagulation', 'heparin- induced', 'donidalorsen- 4', 'Study Day56', the inline footnote marker '48'. Where a sentence is split by a page break I quoted the longest contiguous fragment that carries the claim and put the other fragment in notes rather than silently rejoining them.
- SOURCE_LOCUS: gives the section, the PDF page from the converter's own page markers, and the line range in the converted .txt file. For the two FDA reviews the PDF page and the review's own printed page number differ; both are given.
- FIGURES: no value was read off any plot. Volanesorsen Figures 19-22 (Kaplan-Meier bleeding/platelet curves, exposure-response scatter) and donidalorsen Figures 8-10 (PKK/PPA time courses) contain data that exists ONLY as plotted panels; nothing from them is in this file.
- PLATELET ROWS: 6 rows use readout_category 'platelet_coag_crosstalk'. Every one is admitted only because the source itself ties the platelet observation to a cascade or haemostasis statement in the same sentence (e.g. the FDA reviewer's '<75 x 10^9/L, the level below which primary hemostasis is generally considered to be impaired', or the platelet nadir reported concomitantly with the fatal intracranial haemorrhage). Bare platelet counts, nadir tables (Waylivra Tables 38-39) and thrombocytopenia incidence rates are NOT extracted - they belong to the thrombocytopenia dossier.
- FLAG CONVENTION: on_target_effect=true only where the readout interrogates the drug's own intended pathway (all donidalorsen prekallikrein/PPA/contact-system rows). unintended_toxicity=true where an adverse finding was actually observed; false on measured-null rows, so a null does not read as a positive toxicity signal.
- DELIBERATE DUPLICATION: the inotersen fatal intracranial haemorrhage appears twice (S4 EMA framing, S5 FDA case narrative) because the two regulators publish non-overlapping detail on the same event. Deduplicate on event, not row. Likewise the volanesorsen CS6 bleeding counts appear in both a Table 42 row and a narrative row.
- DERIVED DENOMINATORS: three notes flag denominators I back-calculated from a printed percentage (volanesorsen pooled n=92 from 10/10.9%; donidalorsen Pool 2 n=130 from 12/9.2%). These are marked as derived in the row notes and should not be treated as printed values.
- REDACTIONS: the FDA reviews redact subject identifiers as '(b) (6)'. Quotes reproduce the resulting gaps, e.g. '(Subject )'. Platelet-count tables in the FDA case narratives (Tables 26-27) are partly redacted images.
- ANIMAL DATA PRESENT BUT NOT EXTRACTED (this round is human-only): the Dawnzera AR reports 'minimal, transient prolongations in activated partial thromboplastin time (aPTT) at 30 mg/kg/week' in the monkey repeat-dose study (p.30, text lines 1358-1360) - the only actual aPTT NUMBER-adjacent statement in this whole bundle, and it is animal. The Amvuttra AR reports 'no clinical signs, altered coagulation or most clinical chemistry' changes in repeat-dose toxicity studies (text line 1292). Both are flagged here so the animal-extraction pass can pick them up.
- MODIFICATIONS: 60 per-position rows for the three single-stranded ASOs. Each source publishes per-position chemistry via an explicit case/prefix convention with a stated legend PLUS a complete per-residue IUPAC chemical name (or, for donidalorsen, an explicit S/O linkage shorthand). The underlining that marks the MOE wings is lost in PDF-to-text conversion in all three documents, so the wing/gap boundary was taken from each report's explicit prose statement of the 5-10-5 design, and every base was cross-checked against the chemical name. Reconstructed base strings match the printed sequences at all 20 positions for all three. NO modification rows are emitted for vutrisiran: its per-position chemistry IS published for both strands, but the schema has no strand field and merging a 21-mer sense and a 23-mer antisense strand into one position index would be a fabrication. The vutrisiran letter sequences in the oligos block were transcribed residue-by-residue from the printed chemical names and then verified by confirming complete Watson-Crick pairing of antisense positions 1-21 against sense positions 21-1, leaving the stated 2-nucleotide 3' overhang.
refused_rows:
1. SILENCE ROWS FOR VOLANESORSEN aPTT / PT / TT / FIBRINOGEN / D-DIMER / FACTOR ACTIVITIES. This is the single biggest thing a reader will want from this bundle and I would not manufacture it. The rules require a verbatim quote per row and no sentence in any of the three volanesorsen documents states that these were measured, or that they were normal. They are simply absent. Recorded in extraction_notes as reporting silence instead of as rows, so the gap is visible without a fabricated readout carrying it.

2. VUTRISIRAN CONJUNCTIVAL HAEMORRHAGE (4.1% of vutrisiran subjects, Eye disorders SOC, Amvuttra AR p.125). It is a bleeding event, but the source reports it in an ocular AE listing with no comparator for that preferred term, does not attribute it to any coagulation abnormality, and states in the same report that coagulation parameters were stable. Extracting it as a coagulation-attributable bleeding outcome would misrepresent the source. Same reasoning for the 'recent history of gynecological pain and bleeding' in the malignancy narrative.

3. ALL PLATELET-COUNT-ONLY DATA. Large amounts were available and deliberately left out: Waylivra Table 38 (confirmed nadir platelet counts in CS16), Table 39 (dose, platelet reduction and TG reduction by body weight, including nadir platelet 76 vs 126 x 10^9/L below/above 70 kg), the 68% vs 15% and 75%/47% threshold-crossing rates, the inotersen 55.4% vs 16.7% <140 x 10^9/L rate and 24%/26% mean reductions, and the donidalorsen platelet stability figures. These are the thrombocytopenia endpoint, which has its own dossier. Only the 6 rows where the source itself joins platelets to haemostasis or to a bleed in one sentence were taken.

4. ANY VALUE THAT EXISTS ONLY IN A FIGURE. Waylivra Figure 19 (KM time to platelet threshold), Figure 20 (platelet reduction vs body weight), Figure 21 (largest platelet decrease vs steady-state exposure), Figure 22 (KM time to onset of on-study bleeding AEs) and Dawnzera Figures 8, 9 and 10 (PKK and plasma proenzyme activation time courses) all contain extractable-looking curves. Nothing was read off any of them.

5. FDA TABLE 45 'Study CS2 Hemorrhage Treatment-Emergent Adverse Events' (inotersen Medical Review, PDF p.194). This is the per-preferred-term hemorrhage table that would resolve contradiction (6) above. It survived the PDF conversion as a caption and a source line with NO table body - it is an image. I did not reconstruct it and did not guess which arm the 20.5%/11.7% haematoma figures belong to.

6. VOLANESORSEN BLEEDING-ONSET TIMING PERCENTAGES (AR p.96: '44 (30%) <=13 weeks, 16 (12.5%) >13-26 weeks, and 17 (3.4%) >26 weeks for volanesorsen; 8 (8.3%), 5 (5.6%), 4 (4.9%) for placebo'). The n/% pairs are internally inconsistent (17 events cannot be 3.4% of the same denominator that makes 16 events 12.5%), and section 3.4 restates the same series with different numbers ('<= 13 weeks 29.9% patients; 13-16 weeks 12.5%; > 26 weeks 13.4%', where '13-16 weeks' is itself almost certainly a typo for 13-26). The underlying quantity is real but no defensible value can be extracted. Flagged rather than guessed.

7. DONIDALORSEN AND VUTRISIRAN ANIMAL COAGULATION FINDINGS. Left to the animal pass (see extraction_notes); this round is human-only and the dataset already carries 1,476 animal rows.

8. INOTERSEN AND DONIDALORSEN COMPLEMENT DATA (C3, C5a, Bb). Complement activation is a well-described phosphorothioate class effect and is discussed at length in both reports, but it is not a coagulation-cascade readout under the stated endpoint and was left out rather than smuggled in under 'coagulation'.

9. CS5 PER-ARM DENOMINATORS FOR DONIDALORSEN. The arm sizes (donidalorsen-4, donidalorsen-8, placebo) are recoverable by back-calculation from several printed percentages but are never printed. n_subjects on those rows carries the printed '91 randomised' total instead of a reconstructed per-arm n.
